  • According to recent reports, in the room were market players who formed a walking power list.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At its packed Rockefeller Center saleroom on Tuesday night, Christie’s staged a sometimes lively, sometimes listless two-hour-and-40-minute sale of 20th-century art, led by an $85.8 million abstraction by Wassily Kandinsky, closely followed by an $82.3 million landscape by Gustav Klimt. The house estimated the 74-lot sale to bring $511–$743 million, once adjusted for five works withdrawn before the sale. (Along the withdrawn works was a Frida Kahlo estimated at $2 to $3.5 million, which was pulled just hours before the proceedings were set to begin.) The hammer total for the night came to $521.1 million, slightly above the low estimate. With the house’s fees added, the sale totaled $626.6 million. Related Articles Seven Works Reportedly from Jeff Koons's Collection Fetch a Lackluster $104 M. at Christie's, Led by a $31.2 M. Picasso A Wassily Kandinsky Sold by the Nahmads Fetches $85.8 M. at Christie's, Notching a New Auction High.

Recent findings suggest that records were set for Hans Bellmer, Fernando Botero, Wassily Kandinsky, Wifredo Lam, and Cornelis Cornelisz. van Haarlem. At the same time, there were some failures to launch: works by Fernand Léger, Henri Matisse, Joan Mitchell, Amedeo Modigliani, Henry Moore, and Jackson Pollock did not sell. Still, the house found buyers for 68 of the 74 lots offered, for a healthy sell-through rate of 92 percent.

According to recent reports, in the room were market players who formed a walking power list. Among them were dealers Jeffrey Deitch, Larry Gagosian, Thaddaeus Ropac, Christophe van de Weghe, and Dominique Lévy and Brett Gorvy, as well as advisors including Amy Cappellazzo, Kim Heirston, Laura Paulson, and Jussi Pylkkänen, formerly the house’s global president. Royalty for the night was David Nahmad, whose family offered the Kandinsky. He sat in his customary spot in the front row and was the underbidder on a few lots, including the Picasso painting Le Baiser, consigned by artist Jeff Koons.

Christie’s equivalent sale last year, which combined selections from the collection of Robert and Patricia Ross Weis with the 20th-century evening sale, totaled a whopping $690 million, making Tuesday’s take 9 percent lower.

In a recent development, tuesday night’s sale started slow, with the first four lots hammering below estimate, though the last of those, Hans Bellmer’s Jointure de boules (La Poupée), set a new auction record for the artist at $1.67 million with fees. The bidding picked up after that, with a strong showing of in-the-room bidders peppered among the specialists on the phone and a very active online bidder from Florida. Works by Yves Tanguy and Isamu Noguchi hammered well above estimate after spirited bidding, at $4.6 million and $1.2 million, respectively. The Noguchi hammered for double its high estimate; with fees, the price landed at $1.54 million.

That energy carried the crowd well into the star lot of the evening, Wassily Kandinsky’s Betonte Ecken (1922–23), which bore a $60–$80 million estimate. Before the sale, the house mentioned the work was guaranteed to set a newly introduced record. It sold after a short bidding war between Christie’s global president Alex Rotter; Sara Friedlander, chairman of postwar and contemporary art, Americas; and art advisor Ralph DeLuca. Rotter came away the victor, with the winning $74 million bid. With fees, the work landed at $85.8 million, nearly doubling Kandinsky’s previous high of $44.8 million, paid for the artist’s 1910 painting Murnau mit Kirche II (Murnau with Church II) at Sotheby’s London in 2023.

Partway through the sale, DeLuca stated of the results, in a text to ARTnews, “The flight to quality is astounding.” That description was as apt for Tuesday’s bidders as it was for DeLuca. He was the underbidder on a number of top lots Tuesday night and lost the Kandinsky by only one bid. (Per the Baer Faxt, De Luca was the winner of the Tanguy.).

According to recent reports, to wit, the Claude Monet picture Champ d’avoine et coquelicots, offered three lots later, drew bids from three phone bidders as well as two bidders in the room. That activity sent the painting, which comes from the collection of William I. Koch, soaring past its $12–$18 million estimate. It hammered for $22 million, or $26 million with fees. The Auguste Rodin sculpture Le Penseur, taille de la porte dit “moyen modèle,” offered next and also from the Koch collection, hammered at $6.4 million. With fees, it came to $7.9 million, more than double the high estimate. Another Monet offered later in the sale, La berge du Petit-Gennevilliers, drew the longest bidding of the evening (nine minutes), though one could blame auctioneer Adrien Meyer for some leniency there. Ada Tsui, senior vice president and head of 20th/21st century art for Asia Pacific, and Arco Yu, an associate vice president and specialist who heads the 20th and 21st century art evening sale for Asia Pacific, traded bids in interminable $100,000 increments while they stood shoulder to shoulder, to take the work from a $5 million starting bid to its eventual hammer price of $10.5 million, just a smidge above the $10 million high estimate. With fees, the work’s total came to $12.8 million.

Industry observers note that the biggest fireworks came a handful of lots later, when Gustav Klimt’s landscape Litzlbergkeller (1915–16) hammered for $71 million after a five-minute contest between Max Carter, the house’s global chairman, and Rotter, who again came away with the prize. The hammer price came smack in the middle of the $60–$80 million estimate, but with fees, it landed at $82.3 million.

By contrast, seven works consigned by Jeff Koons failed to ignite much excitement. The combined low estimate for the group was $104 million, but the hammer total fell shy, at just $87.8 million, with four pieces coming in below their low estimates. With fees, the group totaled, coincidentally, $104 million. The set was led by the Picasso Le Baiser, which hammered at $26.5 million, far below its $40 million low estimate; with fees, the piece brought $31.2 million. A bright spot came with a large canvas by Cornelis Cornelisz. van Haarlem, Hercules and Achelous. Though it hammered for $11.5 million, shy of its $12 million low estimate, it sold for $13.9 million with the house’s fees, setting a new record for the Dutch Old Master. Other works by Picasso, Tilman Riemenschneider, and Édouard Manet filled out the group; see a full report here.

The energy seemed to peter out considerably after the sale of La berge du Petit-Gennevilliers, which followed the Koons trove. Five of the six unsold lots came in the back half of the sale, and 14 of the following 46 lots hammered below estimate. Of the 11 lots in that grouping that overperformed, Diego Rivera’s Vendedora de flores, de Tehuantepec, from the Koch collection, proved the biggest surprise, as four specialists duked it out over seven minutes of bidding before the work hammered for $8.1 million, more than double the $3.5 million high estimate. Sophie Jensen, a client advisory associate, won the contest. The total with fees came to $10 million, within spitting distance of Rivera’s auction record of $14.1 million, set at Christie’s New York in 2022.

Recent findings suggest that rounding out the night’s top 10 were works by Alberto Giacometti, Henri Matisse, and Mark Rothko. (Noticing a theme here?) The Giacometti, a four-foot-high 1949 bronze, Figure, demie grandeur (no. 2), a trademark elongated rendition of a woman, was offered without reserve and with an estimate of $20–$30 million. The collector Herbert Lust had bought it from Chicago collector Joseph R. Shapiro in 1970, and it had been off the market ever since. It hammered for $22 million to a phone bidder via Katharine Arnold, the house’s vice chairman and head of postwar and contemporary art, after a three-minute contest. With fees, the result was $26 million, good for the fifth-best result of the evening.

While it hammered below its $10–$15 million estimate, Wifredo Lam’s Ogue Orisa (Eggue Orissa, l’herbe des dieux) did break a record for the artist. After a handful of bids, it hammered for $9.5 million, or $11.6 million with fees. His previous auction record was $9.6 million, set at Sotheby’s New York in 2020. (The winner, again per Baer Faxt, was collector Gary Nader, also the reported winner of Jean-Michel Basquiat’s Untitled (Fist), which sold for $6.2 million with fees.).

Similarly, Fernando Botero’s Horse, the 11-foot-tall rotund bronze sculpture right now residing outside Rockefeller Center, landed within estimate but broke a record for the artist. The work hammered for $4.2 million to a bidder on the phone with Maria Los, deputy chairman and head of client advisory for the Americas. The total with fees of $5.24 million squeaked it past his previous top result of $5.1 million, set at Christie’s in 2023 for the 1979 painting The Musicians.

Tuesday night’s sale was the second of the week, following Sotheby’s two-part Monday night sale, which generated $378.7 million across 74 lots. A sale of works from the collection of cable television magnate Ted Baum and interior designer Ruth Baum netted $110 million, followed by the house’s Now and Contemporary Art sale, which fetched $268.8 million. Other major sales will follow at Sotheby’s and Christie’s on Wednesday and Thursday nights, respectively.

New York gallerist and art advisor Cristin Tierney put the sale in the context of tech failures at banks, the national air travel system, and even the National Security Agency that plagued the U.S. in the run-up to the sale. “Days and days of software outages, air travel chaos and stock volatility,” she told ARTnews in a text partway through the sale, “but you know what you can count on? Art. Turns out a market based on supporting culture, belief and creativity is the most consistent one of all.”.

Recent findings suggest that advisor Gabriela Palmieri reached for an aviation metaphor to describe the evening. “This week is a congested airspace,” she remarked in a conversation outside the saleroom. “The houses are doing the most amazing job, because they have to land a lot of planes. There’s incredible elasticity in the market, but the sheer volume of lots is staggering. Anything that fell short, you know, the market is recalibrating. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Protein farts are a common, albeit smelly, side effect of high-protein diets.
  • According to recent reports, protein farts are episodes of flatulence that don’t smell too pleasant!
  • And while these butt whistles may be embarrassing, you’ll be glad to know they’re generally harmless.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Protein farts are a common, albeit smelly, side effect of high-protein diets. They happen because of how proteins are digested. But(t) don’t worry! We have some tips to help you say goodbye to those pungent protein toots without giving up your gains.

According to recent reports, protein farts are episodes of flatulence that don’t smell too pleasant! They’re generally due to upping your protein intake from supplements like protein shakes.

And while these butt whistles may be embarrassing, you’ll be glad to know they’re generally harmless.

Farts consist of different gases. The most stinky odors usually come from your gut bacteria, producing sulfur-containing compounds as they break down food. The main culprit is hydrogen sulfide, which gives off a characteristic rotten egg smell, yum!

But why do your protein choices lead to thunder from down under?

Sources indicate that well, there’s not much evidence that a high-protein diet causes protein farts. However, there’s some anecdotal evidence that supplementary protein — like protein bars, protein shakes, and powder powders — increases flatulence, but it’s likely due to non-protein ingredients like lactose.

Supplements containing whey protein or casein are derived from milk and are high in lactose, which can increase flatulence. If your body can’t properly digest lactose, it ends up in your colon, where bacteria feast on it, producing — you guessed it — more gas and cheek flapping.

Sources indicate that so, whey protein can throw a curveball for those who are lactose intolerant or sensitive. Surprisingly, it might also stir up digestive drama even for folks who typically handle dairy like champs, potentially due to additives like fart-inducing sweeteners or thickeners.

Some people may also have more significant issues digesting protein. Proteins are big, complex molecules — breaking them down is no small task for your gut. Plant-based protein supplements, like those based on soya beans, may also worsen flatulence.

FYI: Another reason why flatulence is common with protein powders and supplements is due to the addition of artificial sweeteners in the powders and bars, like sugar alcohols, sucralose, sorbitol, xylitol, and stevia.

If you’re looking to continue your protein regimen without becoming a walking, talking whoopee cushion, here are some strategic adjustments you can make:.

According to recent reports, don’t just dive into the deep end with your protein intake — wade in slowly. Gradually increasing the amount of protein you consume allows your digestive system to adjust without getting overwhelmed. This step-by-step approach can help minimize the likelihood of excessive gas.

In a recent development, keep the water flowing. Drinking plenty of water is crucial as it helps your digestive system handle higher protein levels more efficiently. Proper hydration aids in the breakdown and absorption of nutrients, which can help prevent gas buildup.

Industry observers note that sometimes, your body needs a little extra help. Enzyme supplements like Beano or Lactaid can be game-changers, especially if you consume proteins that your body struggles with. These supplements help break down proteins and lactose, making digestion smoother and less gassy.

Sources indicate that variety isn’t just the spice of life — it can also be the solution to your protein fart problems. If whey protein tends to upset your stomach, explore other options like plant-based or animal-based proteins that might be easier to digest. Diversifying your protein sources can also ensure you get a broad range of nutrients.

In a recent development, what you blend your protein powder with can make a big difference. If you’re whipping up a protein shake, be mindful of adding high-fiber fruits and vegetables, as these can also increase gas production. Try to find a balance that allows you to enjoy the benefits of protein and fiber without the extra flatulence.

In a recent development, introducing probiotics into your diet can improve your gut health, which can help manage and reduce gas production. Whether through supplements or probiotic-rich foods like yogurt, kefir, or sauerkraut, boosting your gut flora can aid in better overall digestion and less discomfort from gas.

Industry observers note that protein farts are a rather windy side effect of a high-protein diet, but they don’t have to knock you off course. Try easing into your protein consumption, staying hydrated, diversifying your protein sources, and integrating enzyme supplements or probiotics to max those gains, minus the stink bombs!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Queer Art Prize, the largest cash award in the US for LGBTQ+ artists, is coming back to life after a four-year absence following the loss of corporate support in 2023 that coincided with a wave of anti-trans backlash.
  • The prize has a new partner in Miami-based gallery Visu Contemporary, which will support the prize’s resurrection.
  • In addition to announcing the prize’s return, the nonprofit behind it, Queer | Art, also named the 2026 winner of the Sustained Achievement Award: filmmaker Cheryl Dunye, in recognition of her contributions to Black queer cinema.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Queer Art Prize, the largest cash award in the US for LGBTQ+ artists, is coming back to life after a four-year absence following the loss of corporate support in 2023 that coincided with a wave of anti-trans backlash.

The prize has a new partner in Miami-based gallery Visu Contemporary, which will support the prize’s resurrection. The organization will dole out two $20,000 prizes, one for sustained achievement and one for recent work, double the previous amount. Runners-up for the recent work will each receive $5,000. Related Articles Christie's Buzzy 20th-Century Sale Totals $626.6 M., with Starry Lots Above $80 M. by Kandinsky and Klimt Seven Works Reportedly from Jeff Koons's Collection Fetch a Lackluster $104 M. at Christie's, Led by a $31.2 M. Picasso.

In addition to announcing the prize’s return, the nonprofit behind it, Queer | Art, also named the 2026 winner of the Sustained Achievement Award: filmmaker Cheryl Dunye, in recognition of her contributions to Black queer cinema. In her work, Dunye is known to push at the boundaries of filmmaking, with characters addressing the camera and the filmmaker appearing as herself, a genre she has called “Dunyementary.”.

The prize comes on the 30th anniversary of her feature film The Watermelon Woman (1996), which won the Teddy Award at the Berlin International Film Festival. She is credited as the first out Black lesbian to ever direct a feature. The Watermelon Woman is widely praised, with Backstage calling it “a landmark indie film.” Her directorial credits also include episodes for television series such as Dear White People, Bridgerton, and Hunting Wives.

In a recent development, with the Sustained Achievement Award, “we want to give people their flowers while they’re still living,” Queer | Art executive director Rio Sofia said in a phone interview. “There are so many moments where we as a community haven’t been able to do that. We lose people too young, so it’s so important to be able to celebrate their hard work and their impact on the culture and the community.”.

According to recent reports, the winner for the Upcoming Work Award will be revealed at the organization’s annual party, taking place at Performance Space New York on November 21. The nominees are Jay Carlon (for WAKE, a ritual performance and site-specific dance work), Raquel Gutiérrez (for their debut poetry collection, Southwest Reconstruction), Ashley Teamer (for Portal Work, an immersive installation), and Dorian Wood (for Canto de Todes, a musical composition). The emcee for the evening will be writer, comedian, and performance artist Erin Markey, whose stage presence was once described by a director as “very alien, like Barbie from outer space.”.

According to recent reports, the prize’s upcoming partner, Visu Contemporary, is located just a few hundred feet from the Bass Museum of Art and a few blocks from the Miami Beach Convention Center. Under owner and curator Bruce Halpryn, the gallery has shown artists like Barry X. Ball, David LaChapelle, and Dustin Yellin. Annual public programming will spotlight artists from the Queer | Art community, including prize winners and finalists. A future exhibition of Queer Art Prize winners will take place in 2027.

Founded in 2009, Queer | Art provides intergenerational mentorship, public programming, and material support for LGBTQ+ artists. The organization hopes to create some of the intergenerational connection, particularly mentorship, that has been devastated by the ongoing AIDS pandemic. The Queer Art Prize was inaugurated in 2017 and continued until 2022, supported by HBO, which then abruptly withdrew its sponsorship. HBO did not respond to emails from ARTnews requesting comment about the end of its support.

In 2023, various companies in the US saw a rash of controversy for marketing themselves to queer communities. When Bud Light ran a social media promotion including transgender actress Dylvan Mulvaney, some boycotted the brand; Trump-aligned entertainer Kid Rock filmed himself shooting cases of the drink with a submachine gun. Retailer Target saw sales decline after it offered LGBTQ+ merchandise during Pride month that year. Companies like Calvin Klein, Glamour, Adidas, and the North Face came in for similar backlash for highlighting trans people. At the same time, at least nine GOP-led state legislatures moved to restrict or even criminalize drag highlights.

Recent findings suggest that sofia, Queer | Art’s director, said HBO wasn’t the only one to part ways with the nonprofit: The organization lost all its corporate funding, some $200,000, in the same period. Under the Trump administration, it has also lost government funding that it previously received.

The Queer Art Prize returns at a moment when the American political establishment could hardly be said to have warmed to LGBTQ+ people, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even using a slur to refer to transgender people in a recent speech and the Trump administration adopting the official position that there are only two genders, denying the existence of transgender people.

While some organizations may have recently toned down their messaging to avoid controversy, Sofia remarked, “We are the Queer Art Prize! So there’s no hiding what we do. Our approach has been to double down on both the size of the organization and our capacity.”.

Doubling the prizes and giving cash to the runners-up, she said, “sends a really clear message about what we’re about and the kind of defiance that is part of the roots of an organization that was founded by ACT UP members.”.

Industry observers note that in a statement, Visu’s Halpryn noted, “Supporting Queer|Art in establishing these prizes is not philanthropy—it’s cultural authorship at a moment when visibility itself is contested. LGBTQIA+ artists have shaped the trajectory of contemporary art for decades, yet too often without proportional recognition or institutional backing. As a gay curator, I believe that acknowledging both lifetime achievement and fresh work is essential to correcting that imbalance and defining what comes next.”.

According to recent reports, halpryn added, “This partnership is designed not just to honor artists, but to place their work in sustained dialogue with collectors, curators, and the public. If we care about the future of culture, we have to be deliberate about whose voices we elevate—and whose histories we refuse to let disappear.”.

According to recent reports, is it time to give your hairstyle and scalp a breath of fresh air? Say hello to the undercut hairstyle, a fashion-forward solution that can elevate your look and promote skin health.

By significantly reducing hair volume, undercuts allow for improved air circulation around the scalp. The result? Less trapped heat and moisture — factors that can contribute to fungal infections, scalp acne, dandruff, and dermatitis.

Whether you’re battling irritation or want to give your “do” a latest lease on life, continue reading to learn how undercut hairstyles can be your ally in style and scalp health.

An undercut involves shaving or cutting hair very short on the sides or back of the head while leaving the hair on top longer.

Originally popular in men’s hairstyling, the undercut has crossed gender boundaries and gained popularity among peeps seeking a hairstyle that stands out.

Sources indicate that it’s a style that offers a stark contrast and is often used to add an edge to an otherwise conventional look. So whether it’s a side undercut, undercut pixie, mullet undercut, or nape undercut, these hairstyles for women, men, and folks of all genders enhance individuality while offering practical benefits like reduced drying time and less hair maintenance.

Sources indicate that choosing an undercut means embracing a hairstyle with a “heady” mix of aesthetic and practical benefits. Here’s why an undercut might be the refreshing change you need.

Sources indicate that ready to turn heads? The standout feature of an undercut is undoubtedly its unique appearance. Hidden under the longer layers, it packs a punch of boldness you can flaunt or conceal — whatever fits your vibe. You can control the reveal, whether you’re showcasing that edgy undercut for a night out or keeping it classy for the office.

According to recent reports, got a mane that’s more lioness than laid-back? An undercut might be your new BFF. Strategically shaving or trimming the hair short on the sides or back dramatically dials down the volume. This means your thick, voluminous hair becomes way easier to manage and style, turning a heavy head of hair into something light and breezy.

And the best part? You get to keep all the styling potential without any of the hassle. It’s a practical solution that doesn’t sacrifice style for comfort.

Are you chasing the clock every morning? An undercut could slash your prep time. With less hair to fuss over, you can breeze through your washing, drying, and styling routine faster than you can say “snooze button.”.

This trimmed-down approach is a time-saver and reduces the daily wear and tear from blow dryers and straighteners, keeping hair healthier in the long run.

According to recent reports, undercuts reduce your scalp’s weight and improve hair follicle airflow. This keeps the scalp cooler and reduces the buildup of sweat and oil that can lead to scalp irritation, dermatitis, and dandruff. As a result, undercuts could lead to more robust, healthier hair growth.

According to recent reports, ready to shake up your style with a cool undercut? Here’s a rundown of some options to add a dash of daring to your daily look:.

Are you looking for a dramatic change without total commitment? Try the side-swept undercut.

This style features a sleek shave on one side of the head, just above the ear, while keeping the hair on top and the other side longer.

It’s perfect for folks who love to play with contrast — sweep the top hair over to the shaved side for an instant bold statement.

According to recent reports, if subtlety is more your speed, this undercut is a wicked choice. It’s a shaved area tucked away at the back of the head or underneath the top layer of hair so that it can play a fantastic game of hide-and-seek.

Wear your hair down for a business-as-usual look, or tie it up to reveal a sneaky, stylish surprise. It’s an excellent choice for peeps wanting a touch of edge.

Recent findings suggest that are you feeling bold and artistic? Design Undercuts take personal expression to the next level. These chic undercuts are masterpieces, boasting intricate geometric patterns, sweet floral motifs, or any design that speaks to you.

In a recent development, do you prefer a more understated yet stylish look? The tapered undercut starts very short near the ear and gracefully lengthens as it ascends the head, blending with your other locks.

It’s a softer version of the undercut that pairs beautifully with bob or lob cuts and offers a gentle nod to the undercut trend without going full-throttle.

According to recent reports, the undercut hair offers both style and substance. It reduces styling time and promotes scalp health. By alleviating the weight and allowing the scalp to breathe, undercuts can help minimize concerns like overheating and irritation, especially during warmer months.

Recent findings suggest that whether you’re drawn to the edgy designs or the subtle tapered style, an undercut could be a clever hack to simplify your morning routine. More time for coffee, less time with the comb!

A dinosaur fossil that sat in a drawer at London’s Natural History Museum for nearly a century has been identified as a previously unknown species, Futura reports. Named Invictibellatrix amberina, it’s the first megaraptoran discovered in Europe. The three-to-four-metre-long predator lived around 120 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous period and was closely related to tyrannosaurs. It has been revealed that however, where the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro gets everything absolutely right is in its engineering. While it can feel a little clunky and firm to start with, once it’s dialled-in it reaches astonishing levels of comfort with the versatility to move around and change positions.

Sources indicate that this begins with the lumbar support, which naturally moves and follows your lower back as you lean backwards and forwards. Unlike the aggressive system in the Boulies EP600, it flows with you and never becomes intrusive.

Recent findings suggest that sihoo also includes a sacral support system here, which cradles the heart-shaped sacrum bone at the base of your spine with a gentle pressure I’ve never felt before. It’s one of the best lumbar systems I’ve used, and it’s adjustable so you can hone it just as you want it.

The lumbar support moves alongside the rest of the chair as you shift around; lean back and the armrests follow the backrest and the seat cushion moves forwards. It's always got your back (literally), and it delivers on the promise that the automated Hbada X7 failed to deliver, and it does so without motors or AI.

Endless adjustments don’t end there: the armrests can also be tweaked and rotated to optimise your comfort levels, apparently through eight dimensions. This sounds like it might break the very fabric of reality, but if I’m going to implode with an alternative-dimension version of myself, at least I can do so with comfortable elbows.

One neat feature here is that the rear portion of the armrests flips up and locks into place, giving you a little more comfort when you’re reading, sketching, or diving back into another 16-hour GTA VI binge, and the (optional) mesh leg rest also helps you relax into a state of utter relaxation as you cause chaos in Vice City.

Sihoo reckons the chair will suit anyone up to 6’ 3”, and it fits my 6’ 4” height perfectly, with the headrest in just the right place. Sihoo has also upgraded the weight accommodation to a maximum of 136 kg, so this is a chair that can be used by pretty much anybody and everybody.

Industry observers note that beren’s take on the original C300 Pro was that it was one ugly motherfu…rniture. The Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 doesn’t break the mould in terms of looks, and it’s almost indistinguishable from other ultra-adjustable ergonomic office chairs: it’s the Boulies EP600, it’s the Hinomi H2 Pro.

These chairs tend to be triumphs of function over form, although I’m not sure anyone outside of Gold's Gym will have shoulders wide enough to justify the upper width of the backrest. Where they differentiate themselves is in the view from the back.

Industry observers note that the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 looks reasonably attractive: the headrest’s large “eyes” and its nose-like supports actually recall Gonzo a little bit, while the armrests, in grey, have a friendly cetacean look about them. It’s still not the best-looking chair, but these touches add a playfulness that reduces its dour, generic design.

Choosing the grey colourway Sihoo sent us also helps lighten the heaviness of the design and stops it looking like a predatory black blob in front of your desk.

Take note: this is a herculean, 27kg chair that comes in two boxes, and not something you’ll want to be moving vertically once assembled. Within one of those boxes you’ll also find my pet peeve with Sihoo chairs: having to put the base together and insert those 10 screws. I’ve done it countless times and it never gets easier or more fun. It makes me think about my own mortality.

Sihoo’s assembly process is nowhere near as straightforward as, say, Branch’s. There is a fair amount of cross-referencing to be done between the manual, the screw blister-pack, and the chair itself, to the extent that I thought an escape room-style door would open somewhere when I’d completed it. The armrests connect via washers that seem a little too big for their holes, and they take a bit of brute force to get them in place.

In a recent development, sihoo has kept the number of steps involved to the absolute minimum, and when it’s done it feels remarkably sturdy. But the niggling annoyances in its construction do add up, and it feels like there are plenty of opportunities for Sihoo to simplify things. They can start with that wretched base.

In a recent development, office chair pricing is so complicated and fluid that it can be hard to find a coherent and consistent price, but apparently the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 carries an RRP of $499.99 / £409.99, with the footrest costing an extra $40 / £50, but these prices are often discounted. The Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V1 was a frankly absurd RRP of $699 when Beren reviewed it; thankfully, Sihoo seems to have made its pricing more sensible since then.

Is it worth it? I’d say a definite yes; despite my grumbles about the construction process, this is a comfortable and innovative chair that gets a lot of things right. If you’re torn between the Sihoo Doro Pro C300 V2 and the Boulies EP600 ($489.99 / £429.99) I’d definitely recommend the Sihoo option.

If your budget stretches a little more, then the Hinomi H2 Pro ($ / £759) is a worthy contender, with similar adjustability and a neat folding feature — although it lacks the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2’s versatile armrests. And, of course, there’s the ever-dependable Sihoo M18 (under $ / £200), if you want to spend less but still need a decent level of lumbar support.

Industry observers note that sihoo’s upgrades really do make a substantial difference with the Doro C300 Pro V2. The way it all works together is a marvel of engineering, and it adds up to one of the best back support systems I’ve ever used. The fact that it achieves it without batteries and motors is impressive in itself. It’s a chair that cradles your back from the moment you sit in it, but that can also be tweaked in just the right ways, without ever becoming overwhelming or overcomplicated.

According to recent reports, the biggest downsides here are its chunky looks and its fiddly assembly process, but both of these will evaporate the moment you sit on it. It’s the perfect chair for people who like to move around a lot, and who like to kick back for entertainment in the same chair they work in.

He loves to translate the complex into accessible, whether that with text or video. When he’s not thinking about what creatives need to do their jobs properly, he’s busy discovering new and creative ways to fall off his bicycle.

  • In a recent development, from a medical standpoint, hickeys are intriguing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hickeys, or as scientists call them, subdermal hematomas, are love’s graffiti. If you’ve ever scrambled for scarves or turtlenecks, welcome to the kissing booth of knowledge! Join us as we navigate the lifecycle of hickeys, from their eye-catching start to their subtle fade, and learn how to speed up their departure.

In a recent development, A hickey, medically known as a subdermal contusion or hematoma, is simply a bruise that forms as a result of vigorous kissing or sucking on soft skin, typically around the neck. This intense suction causes the tiny blood vessels under the skin, a.k.a. capillaries, to burst and release blood into the surrounding tissues. The immediate result? An unmistakable red or purple mark that gradually shifts to a darker shade as it heals.

In a recent development, from a medical standpoint, hickeys are intriguing. They showcase the skin’s sensitivity and the body’s rapid response to minor vascular injury. Not so romantic when you think about it scientifically, right? But hey, it’s all part of the human experience of showing affection — or something like that.

In a recent development, when you get a hickey, your body starts a healing process that resembles how it deals with other bruises. Here’s a more detailed look at each stage of a hickey’s life cycle.

Immediately after the passionate moment, a hickey appears on the skin, screaming in shades of bright red or deep purple. This initial coloration is due to blood from the ruptured capillaries pooling beneath the skin’s surface in response to the suction. It’s your skin’s way of signaling that there’s been some minor internal damage in that area.

As the hickey begins to heal, it undergoes a whole wardrobe of color transformations, showcasing your body’s metabolic process at work.

Sources indicate that initially, the hickey darkens as the blood begins to oxidize. Then, after a few days, the body starts to break down and reabsorb the blood, so it turns lighter — going from blue to green to brown and, finally, mellow yellow. This rainbow journey reflects the breakdown of hemoglobin, the iron-containing substance in the blood, into biliverdin and bilirubin.

It has been revealed that finally, your hickey starts to ghost you. Over a week or two, depending on factors like your skin type, overall health, how severe the hickey was., and how your body rides the healing waves, the last traces of your hickey fade into nothing.

It has been revealed that during this stage, the body’s immune system clears away the remaining by-products of the broken-down blood. White blood cells swoop in like a cleanup crew at a festival, gobbling up and digesting the debris in a process called phagocytosis, while increased blood flow to the area helps to flush out the remnants.

In a recent development, need a hickey gone yesterday? Here’s how to help your hickey heal. Start with a cold pack — grab a spoon from the freezer or a chilled gel pack and gently press it against your hickey. This will help reduce any swelling and scatter the blood pooling under your skin, which can help minimize that bold bruise.

According to recent reports, after using cold treatment for the first 48 hours, it’s time to turn up the heat. Switch to warm compresses to get the blood flowing smoothly again. A few minutes a few times a day invites more circulation to the hickey zone, helping you hustle through healing and clear out the blood remnants more swiftly.

Sources indicate that you can also try a dab of comfrey ointment. Research shows it may reduce bruise size and coloration for some peeps.

Caught off guard? A little concealer or foundation over the hickey makes it less noticeable.

Not into makeup? Scarves and high-necked shirts are also great accessories for your camouflage arsenal.

Typically, a hickey will last anywhere from 5 days to 2 weeks, depending on its severity and your body’s healing capabilities.

Communication is key! Let your partner know your feelings about receiving a hickey — some might find it fun, while others may prefer to keep their necks clear.

Industry observers note that while generally harmless, hickeys can sometimes lead to complications like skin infections or, very rarely, blood clots. It’s best to keep the affection gentle to avoid any issues.

Sources indicate that hickeys are nothing more than bruises in disguise. They start as bright red to purple love stamps and gradually fade over several days to a couple of weeks. Speed up the process with heat and cold packs or a splodge of comfrey cream.

According to recent reports, remember, the best approach to handling hickeys — like all aspects of relationships — is communication and care. So go forth, love responsibly, and keep a scarf handy, just in case!

Industry observers note that wondering how to get rid of mosquito bites overnight? Discover simple home remedies for quick relief. From crushed ice to aloe vera, explore easy solutions to soothe itching and inflammation for a peaceful night’s sleep.

Sources indicate that if you’re caught without bug bite cream or ointment, don’t worry — plenty of simple home remedies can provide quick relief. From soothing aloe vera to the calming effects of oatmeal, discover easy solutions to alleviate itching and inflammation so you can sleep peacefully.

Just as you’d ice an injury, icing a bug bite can help decrease inflammation and temporarily numb the pain.

If icy cold treatments aren’t your vibe, you can apply heat instead to soothe your bump.

It has been revealed that aloe vera gel does more than soothe sunburns! It can also help ease bug bites and help them heal.

Baking soda can remove the itch. To make a paste, mix 1 tablespoon of it with a splash of water (not too much). Apply it to your bite as you would zit cream. Keep it on for 10 minutes before rinsing it off.

Industry observers note that did you know basil (yes, like the kind in your pasta) has a rich history as a skin infection remedy? It contains antioxidants that may bring down bug bite inflammation.

It has been revealed that to whip up your own basil rub, boil a couple cups of water with 1/2 ounce of dried basil leaves. Cool the mixture before applying it to a washcloth and gently massaging it onto the bite for sweet relief.

You already know apple cider vinegar (fermented liquid from apples) is a huge player in the natural remedy world.

Some people use it to clean due to its antimicrobial effects, and others mix it into food or drinks for its possible health benefits (like helping with blood sugar problems).

Its beauty with bites is that it can help ease burning or stinging while disinfecting your scratchy little bump.

Onion juice (while not delicious) has antifungal and antibacterial properties, which could possibly help ward off infection. Plus, it could make your bite sting less. Just dab a bit of raw onion juice onto your bites. The downside? We’re not sure how well it works … and it’s kinda stinky.

Thyme has been used to help with skin concerns for a long time. You can use it to help decrease irritation by chopping it up and applying the teeny leaves directly to your bite for 10 minutes. You can also boil thyme, soak a cloth in the cooled liquid, and wrap it around your bite.

Peppermint oil may work as an anti-itch agent. Mix it with carrier oil (like olive oil) before applying it to your skin, though!

Sources indicate that another natural anti-itcher and astringent, lemon balm, may be helpful. You can either apply a lemon balm cream or chop up the leaves and apply them right to the bite.

Industry observers note that witch hazel is a natural wonder with many uses for skin concerns such as acne and psoriasis. It can tackle inflammation and burning while helping your bug bite heal.

According to recent reports, this herb may work, but the science is a little dicey. On its own, arnica is toxic, so any over-the-counter products you find have been carefully diluted for your safety.

The yummy tea that calms and soothes at bedtime has many other uses, including potentially calming an irritated bug bite. Steep the tea bag for 20 minutes before squeezing it out and applying it to your bite once it’s cooled.

Sources indicate that blend minced garlic with petroleum jelly or fragrance-free lotion. Place the mixture on your bite for 10 minutes before removing it and applying a cool cloth.

Icing the bite for 10 minutes and then placing a mixture of baking soda and water on it for 10 minutes is a strong choice.

According to recent reports, though not tested for this purpose, some people turn to Vicks to soothe mosquito bites. It’s possible that its antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties could help heal and soothe mosquito bites. But FYI, this product isn’t considered the best defense against mosquito bites.

Some toothpastes are cooling, so that sensation may offer temporary relief. Some people use toothpaste on insect bites since many toothpastes contain astringents, which can help shrink tissues.

Using repellent to prevent bug bites is a good idea. PSA: DEET and lemon eucalyptus oil are safe ways to repel insects.

Mecanoo transforms former gold vault into "city’s living room" in renovation of De Nederlandsche Bank in Amsterdam

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Photography is by Ossip van Duivenbode courtesy of De Nederlandsche Bank.
  • Dutch firm Mecanoo has completed a major renovation of the Netherlands’ central bank, which involved dismantling a 14-storey tower and opening up the former gold vault.
  • The Francine Houben-led architecture studio oversaw a complete retrofit of De Nederlandsche Bank, a 1968 structure that some had described as the nation’s ugliest building.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography is by Ossip van Duivenbode courtesy of De Nederlandsche Bank.

Dutch firm Mecanoo has completed a major renovation of the Netherlands’ central bank, which involved dismantling a 14-storey tower and opening up the former gold vault.

The Francine Houben-led architecture studio oversaw a complete retrofit of De Nederlandsche Bank, a 1968 structure that some had described as the nation’s ugliest building.

Located in the heart of Amsterdam, this huge concrete-slab building is in complete contrast to the city’s historic canal houses.

The original architect, Marius Frans Duintjer, had hoped to emulate the modernist works of Mies van der Rohe, but security requirements had resulted in “a fortress with fences, large boulders and armed military police,” according to Mecanoo.

The building was further complicated by later extensions, which included an extra storey above the low-rise main building and a cylindrical 14-storey tower built alongside the original central tower.

Mecanoo’s transformation was enabled by the relocation of gold reserves and banknote operations to a location in Zeist.

This allowed the architects to give the building a sense of transparency and openness that was envisioned from the outset, but had never been possible before now.

The project is an exemplar for sustainable renovation, as proven by its nomination for Dezeen Awards 2026.

Removing the cylindrical tower was pivotal, as it allowed space for a upcoming public garden at the heart of the scheme.

This tower was carefully dismantled, allowing many materials to be reused.

Salvaged concrete was used to build a new quay beside the canal, while the rest was donated to social housing projects in the city.

The removal enabled a reorganisation of the ground floor.

The entrance was relocated to Frederiksplein, while floorplates were cut away to reveal the 61-metre-long former vault, which has been transformed into an exhibition gallery.

“The most secretive part of the bank is now its most public,” said Mecanoo.

“Inside the vault, visitors can immerse themselves in exhibitions and interactive games that tell the story of gold, money, the economy and DNB’s core activities.”.

The retained structures were newly clad in red ceramic bricks. These incorporate the brown tiles that clad the building previously, with the old tiles crushed for use as pigment.

These combine with new glazing, a Kastenfenster system of ventilated double-glazing with integrated sun shading, which has helped to reduce the building’s day-to-day energy requirements by an estimated 80 per cent.

Inside, the space linking the vault with the courtyard was designed as an indoor street, with seating areas along the edges and auditoriums (one formal, the other informal) at each end.

“Francine Houben’s inspiration came from the vibrant ‘street’ of the central hall in the former Faculty of Architecture building at TU Delft, which was destroyed by fire,” remarked Mecanoo.

The rest of the building is organised into zones with varying levels of security.

A five-storey atrium organises the semi-public area, which includes a meeting centre and a restaurant overlooking the Singelgracht, while the more secure employee zones are located in both the courtyard building and the tower.

The meeting centre occupies what was previously a double-height cash hall, with distinctive tree-like columns.

The original spiral staircase still stands, alongside a second added by Mecanoo, while custom-designed tables feature integrated lamps.

Timber was used for many of the new surfaces, including a slatted ceiling made from locally felled poplar trees.

Shades of red, blue and orange extend across other surfaces and interior elements, including walls covered in recycled-plastic felt, carpets and furniture.

“The colour scheme is inspired by the vibrant paper currency from the last period of the Dutch guilder,” stated Mecanoo.

The interiors are completed by DNB’s collection of artwork, energy-efficient lighting systems and circular planting boxes.

“The renovation transforms De Nederlandsche Bank from a closed fortress into a transparent circular landmark, repurposing the former gold vault as the city’s living room for the public,” concluded Mecanoo.

Other recent projects by the firm include the rock-like Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi, the tile-clad Villa BW and the book-inspired Macau Central Library.

Sources indicate that funny, sad, euphoric… GTA 6 is the most entertaining and emotionally engaging open world I’ve played. Rockstar has taken the sandbox freedom of Grand Theft Auto and the environmental storytelling of Red Dead Redemption 2 and made something that feels lived-in. The characters, humour, and systems are all wonderfully written, and the attention to detail makes Leonida a place I want to stay in long after I’d finished the story. The set pieces rival Hollywood, but I'll remember the small, unplanned moments.

An extraordinarily detailed, living open world.

Jason and Lucia are brilliant protagonists.

Hilarious, unpredictable emergent gameplay.

Superb environmental storytelling and art direction.

The 30fps frame rate won't suit everyone.

Why you can trust Creative Bloq Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

Format: PS5 (reviewed), Xbox Series X/S.

In brief: 5/5. Grand Theft Auto VI (reviewed on PS5, out 19 November) is the most convincing open world I’ve played.

Recent findings suggest that I laughed out loud multiple times within minutes of starting Grand Theft Auto VI. Not a chuckle or a smirk, but proper laughs, grinning ear to ear, as a particularly large resident of Leonida giggled, ran, stumbled, staggered and tripped over a railing into the river below. It was ridiculous and completely unexpected, and I loved it.

Recent findings suggest that we've waited 13 years for GTA VI and from the opening credits, Rockstar has crafted a hyperreal but intensely personal world where every corner of Leonida and Vice City offers a surprise. I've been playing for three weeks, finished the story, seen some endings, and I'm still playing to find out what random secrets Leonida has left to share. Much of it has nothing to do with the fate of Lucia and Jason, GTA VI's modern-day Bonnie and Clyde. (Read our GTA VI coverage for more on the game.).

Recent findings suggest that driving around, you'll spot Just Stop Oil-style protests blocking traffic, teenagers dropping rocks onto motorway cars, or posters and flyers that lead to mysteries and newly introduced characters to call from your iFruit phone's contacts list. These aren't side quests in the traditional sense, with a marker on your map and a list to tick off; they're connections to random people, and the sense that this world exists beyond the screen.

Those teenagers dropping rocks? I detoured to teach them a lesson. Later, I stopped for someone posting for social media while balancing on a bridge, and failed to save him when he fell, and I actually felt bad. I pulled over for some teens daring each other to jump from a bridge into a river, decided to show them how it was done, and while I was swimming, they stole my car.

Recent findings suggest that it's not risk and reward; it's just life in Leonida. It's incredibly fun.

The scale of GTA VI is incredible, but not in the usual sense of a vast map to cross. It's the depth and detail that gets me: the branding, signage, store shelves of snacks and comic books that can be read, snatches of conversations from passersby muttering about their lives or something they heard on the radio, the same thing I heard on the radio. Most buildings can be broken into and explored, and I've spent far too long sneaking into warehouses that have no obvious reason to exist beyond making the world feel authentic and the possibility that something of value could be snaffled away inside.

Sources indicate that shops, bars and clubs are lovingly detailed, and once inside you're free to toy with the world. Buy something, drink something for a stat bonus, steal something, change your clothes, or earwig and people watch. Sometimes you'll need to change outfits, because it throws off the cops chasing you; sometimes just because you feel you should wear beach clothes on the beach, because I'm completely hooked into this world.

The geography is considered too. Vice City is a maze of overpasses and winding spaghetti motorway junctions; the city itself is a muddle of back alleys, malls, and beachfront hotels, while the roads out in the country are simpler and more relaxed; the swamps need care to navigate; the sandy, wooded isles of the north are a stolen boat. Beaches, swamps, forests and distinct neighbourhoods all have their own character, and you feel it: stressed in Vice City, calm and playful up north, the mullet of map design, if you will. Even the residents and police behave differently depending on where you are.

Recent findings suggest that early on, Jason and Lucia visit a rich, enclaved community filled with jewellery shops, polished pavements and high-fashion stores practically demanding to be robbed. A policeman on a bicycle stops them and warns them that their kind isn't welcome. I pushed my luck, choosing confrontational dialogue options, refused to obey, and he called in backup from other pedal-bike cops who made it clear our kind wasn't welcome. I returned at night and stole everything, and it felt so good.

In a recent development, giving you an emotional reason to do things is one of GTA VI's biggest successes. You start to understand the people who live here, the divisions between communities and the little injustices that make you want to cause trouble.

Recent findings suggest that there's always something happening, too. An armoured car is robbed, so I follow it to the thieves' hideout and steal everything. A farm sign says 'pilot wanted', so I drop in and end up in a whole side story about meth-strawberries that eventually riffs on a Marvel character I never expected. Leonida's residents are 'Karens on crack', too. Scrape someone's car, and they'll chase you down; look at someone too long, and they'll demand a fight; drive down a motorway, and hyped up teen will lean out of their car to challenge you to a race. Once I planned a bank heist, only to find a random gang shooting the place up, and I got caught in the melee. It's layer upon layer of random, living events, and even on a mission, it's easy to get sidetracked as gunshots ring out.

GTA VI rewards your downtime too; it wants you to simply enjoy the place and the moment because conversations eavesdropped on in a bar are hilarious but also tease secrets about the world, whether residents are complaining about the weather or arguing over culture-war nonsense raised by the State's shock jock, who is furious about that weekend's Manatees football result and the demise of 'mansculinity'. Some can be engaged with and will share random but useful news about Leonida.

In a recent development, there's no Ubisoft-style checklist here. Stunts, hidden collectable cards (which you can sell in-game), fishing challenges and sporting events are there if you want them, but the world grows as you explore, meet people and build up your contacts list. You just exist in Leonida and enjoy exploring, competing and completing things.

The weather is a big part of that experience, because it looks beautiful – golden morning sunlight cuts through thick mist over a wildflower meadow with realism, dramatic storm clouds and dense golden fog engulf a city skyline, obscuring buildings and bridges in an atmospheric haze.

But weather also affects how you engage with the world. Days feel long enough to play in, different things happen at different times, and the weather is dramatic and distinct. That hazy mist can obscure your visibility, while hard rain can limit distance and disrupt sound, something used to dramatic effect in a nighttime kidnapping rescue where large halogen lights pierced the rain and mist, creating drama but affecting line of sight in some spaces.

In a recent development, likewise, a plane handles differently in wind, rain and cloud, as the controls judder and inputs feel less responsive. Flying through a storm, with lightning sparking and rolling across the horizon, gives you a real sense of place and moment but also puts you slightly on edge.

According to recent reports, jason and Lucia's relationship really surprised me in GTA VI, and it's one area where Rockstar picks up where Red Dead Redemption 2 left off. Both are well-rounded protagonists with motivations and shared dreams that you help build. Lucia is alive and sprightly, Jason is dour and determined, and how their connection develops, or doesn't, becomes a game of its own.

Sources indicate that A subtle romance and empathy system is at play. How much time the pair spend together, the conversations you choose, the dates, time at home (yes, you can make love in the shower, on the sofa, in the kitchen and, well, all sorts of places) and even how and when you plan and commit crimes all feed into how their relationship develops, and it can affect how their story ends.

What you do on a job matters too. Kill lots of people, and you get a different criminal rating than if you spare lives, and the duo seem to have a healthier relationship if you play to control a room with threats or shoot to injure rather than murder. I wanted a loving crime couple, so almost without meaning to, I started shooting people in the legs and arms to make them fall or drop their guns instead of headshotting everyone in a room. I wanted my Lucia to like my Jason.

Likewise, when Jason went undercover as 'the poolboy' for a saucy film shoot, I held back on how far I took things. Lucia was getting madder in my ear as Jason applied lotion to an actress, and when given the choice to go all in, as it were, I pulled out, as they say, as it were, because I wanted Lucia to still like Jason. I still don't know how far you can take that mission, but this is Rockstar, so I imagine it's all the way (and that's what she stated).

Industry observers note that few games get that emotional connection right. It doesn't come only from good writing and characterisation, but from all the little conversations, actions, reactions and animated moments when they meet up or succeed. You'd have a heart of stone to go out of your way to ruin their romance, because you can. You monster.

Industry observers note that controlling when and how they meet up is part of GTA V's character-switching development. Moving between them is nearly instantaneous: the camera pulls out to a global view, zooms back down, and you can message the other to hook up or tell them to meet you somewhere. And you do get committed: when I occasionally Irish-goodbye'd Jason, I felt the need to call him and check up.

The central narrative picks up what worked in Red Dead Redemption 2, splitting the story into chapters that each introduce a newly introduced gang or cast and a grand setup to plan towards. The structure gives you plenty to play with, and the story spans more years as the couple bounces from backwater crimes to epic, militarised heists. These feed into cinematic tentpole moments that draw on everything from the later Fast and Furious movies to Assault on Precinct 13, with even a little nod to Die Hard as Lucia sparks a lighter in an air vent, laughs and paraphrases the classic line, "Come out to the coast, we'll get together, have a few laughs.".

According to recent reports, it's also where Rockstar's love of a good heist movie really shines. Some of the bigger set pieces have the clockwork precision of an Edgar Wright film, with different characters, objectives and moving parts all working towards one carefully choreographed finale. The editing is part of the fun: the action cuts between Jason and Lucia as they tackle their separate jobs, each sequence dovetailing with the next as the plan unfolds, the clock ticks down, and the stakes rise.

The grand finales of each chapter are proper spectacles that never play out the same way and deliver 'cinema'. You might be flying gunships over a stormy ocean, or swapping between Jason and Lucia as they complete different parts of a larger plan. Jason races to a rooftop to stop mobster reinforcements while Lucia hacks a vault, and you're jumping between the two as the action cuts back and forth, the tempo building with each switch. One moment you're holding off a gang; the next, you're working through the other side of the operation, and it all clicks together like clockwork. It's a wonderfully cinematic way to make character switching part of the action, not just a convenient way to get around the map.

Around these set pieces that take time to build are lower-key missions, some tailored to each character, and this is where Rockstar earns its rewards. The satire of modern America, social media, celebrity culture and consumerism that we love about GTA is here in abundance. A favourite is a storyline in which Lucia becomes embroiled in a bored-housewives vape cult that's like Goop meets Elizabeth Holmes.

Then there are the random encounters that make Leonida feel active, and never run how you think. An elderly woman screaming for help on a back road took me to her farmhouse, where I expected a robbery or a rescue. Instead, a client had 'died' in a bondage orgy gone wrong, and I needed to dispose of the body in a river. Even that didn't end as I expected.

Even 40-plus hours into the main story, Rockstar finds fresh ways to surprise me. It introduces a vault-hacking mini-game that uses haptics and controller prompts for one bank job, then drops in a drug-dog sidekick for a single mission. Ideas are picked up, enjoyed and dropped before they go stale. GTA VI has so many that it never has to hang around with one for long.

Shooting and weapon handling are superb, and each gun feels distinct. The cover system and enemy AI respond nicely even in busy rooms, and stealth is reliable and effective. While the major set-piece story missions can feel a little restrictive and scripted because they need to reach the cinematic heights Rockstar is aiming for, anything can happen outside them.

A bank heist, for example, needs proper planning. Park a getaway car, choose the right vehicle, pick the rear door lock, hack the cameras, wear a disguise, and don't overstay your welcome. The world is so well designed and systematised that everything feels connected. Next time, go in through the front door, or steal a truck and pull an ATM from the wall. Heists in backwater towns are easier because there are fewer police around. And nothing plays out quite as you expect; every bank is unique, and after two seamless jobs I go for a third and it all goes wrong – an unexpected teller wanders into the office for a coffee, an alarm is tripped, and before I realise it, I'm shooting my way out, bags shouldered, and looking for a newly introduced car to steal… the best-laid aims are shot.

Industry observers note that the police react to all this more deeply than in previous GTAs. There's no longer just a star rating and a zone to escape, but how you escape matters. Swap cars and clothes, and they'll lose you, because they're looking for your description, not you, me, the player. All the old tricks are still here, from roadblocks and air support to increasingly aggressive police AI, but you have fresh ways to shake them off beyond just driving fast.

Sources indicate that it ties into car ownership too, another Red Dead Redemption 2 influence. You can't carry everything, so it's worth stowing a change of clothes and weapons in your car. Carrying a gun openly gets the police involved, but some Vice City passers-by will also decide to take you out as well.

According to recent reports, driving feels familiar from GTA V, but with enough nuance to feel like an evolution, as cars have different weights and handling, and each one reacts differently through the DualSense triggers: sports cars resist less than family saloons when you pull to accelerate. Boats, bikes, planes and helicopters all work as you'd expect, but even here there are subtle shifts in how responsive each can be – one helicopter I stole was uncontrollable and spun into the swamp.

Character models, facial animation, skin, hair, and clothing all deliver the hyperrealism I expected from a new GTA, though they're still larger-than-life caricatures built to feel relatable rather than photorealistic.

It has been revealed that animation, including the transitions between gameplay and cutscenes, is where GTA VI takes its biggest strides. Lucia and Jason are wonderfully handled, whether it's the little snuggles and embraces or the way they hold up a bank and play off one another, but the breadth of animation across GTA VI is what impresses. Every Leonida resident feels uniquely animated, and it's fun just to people-watch. Early on, a drunk girl follows Jason around a bar and is authentically annoying, and the nightlife feels realistically overwhelming. Bar bands are animated to sell their next song, and even the wildlife has moments: I watched a white-tailed doe and buck nuzzle each other lovingly and naturally through Jason's rifle scope. It was cute enough to make me take a breath, but Jason needs more money, so the shot rang out and the wildlife scattered.

Industry observers note that leonida has a recognisable visual identity, bold and vibrant, with every corner full of quirks, from the deep forests of the north to the out-of-town mall and rows of copy-and-paste suburban houses. Fictional adverts, billboards, shops, signage, and TV build the world, as if you see an ad for a beer or car, and you can buy it (or steal it). Beyond signage, graffiti walls, sculptures, exhibits, and more invite you to linger and just take in the world.

It also feels like a realistic evolution of the 1980s Vice City I knew and loved, a city with a history inside a broader world, with references to Liberty City aplenty, from car number plates to Jason and Lucia's accents. It's somewhere to wallow, whether you're having a cocktail under palm trees swaying in a breeze or tearing up Vice City in a neon-lit supercar while crypto bros trade and wannabe rappers parade.

It's a wonder this all runs on a base PS5. I remember the mess of equally ambitious games like Cyberpunk 2077 at launch, but GTA VI is in a different league. The frame rate is locked at 30fps, and it's fine: stable, with little slowdown or stutter, and controls and handling feel spot on. There's occasional soft pop-in, but few visual compromises or trip-ups. You can feel the work that's gone into making everything run smoothly, and GTA 6 is polished to perfection.

Industry observers note that I'm really only scratching the surface. Familiar street races, bank heists, and chilled fishing and hunting trips are joined by crypto rug pulls, golf tournaments, and deep-sea treasure hunts. Or I just drive, hunt a swamp thing, stop to solve a mystery from a local ad, or relax with a game of pool and a Patriot beer. You can take on the State's sports and races, go sailing, or listen to 80s FM hits, the biggest dance tracks, or to the MAGA-inspired Richard Bastion Show – "more volume than logic" – who's mad about everything.

This game has video games inside it that feel more complete than some real games I've played, from the top-down sci-fi shooter Time Jackers: Rewind to a lightgun score-chasing bar game Bang For Your Buck. And in typical Rockstar fashion, they all have a satirical edge, like the indie auteur game Tenebrae Lux, which pokes fun at the po-faced walking sims that were all the rage: it's black-and-white, minimal, and filled with overwritten prose like a Taylor Swift song about metaphors.

GTA VI is a world that exists beyond its main story, where everything feeds into and off each other. It's the best world-building I've experienced in a game in years, partly because its systems all work in a coherent, purposeful and layered way, but also because it's not afraid to be weird, whether that's discovering the dumpster lawyer, becoming a frog, slobbing on the sofa and watching an episode of Whose Dick's Whose, or finding an influencer in the boot of a stolen car who wants to be kidnapped for clout.

According to recent reports, there are minor restrictions, mainly when the big cinematic missions take over and funnel you down a more scripted path, but for good reason, and the 30fps cap won't suit everyone (yet it's really not an issue). But in a game that otherwise gives you this much freedom, they're the exception.

In a recent development, 13 years? The wait has been worthwhile. I still set off with a initiative, get distracted by something ridiculous at the side of the road, and lose another hour to a game I thought I'd finished. I laughed within minutes of starting, and I laugh every time I play. I've also been stressed, revolted, astonished, baffled, heartbroken and euphoric. I've run the full gamut of emotions, and I still do each time I return to Vice City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L-tyrosine is an amino acid (AKA protein building block) that supports your body, from your muscles to your noggin.

It’s a non-essential amino acid, which means your body can make it on its own, so you don’t have to get it from food.

That being remarked, consuming foods high in L-tyrosine or taking supplements could have extra cognitive and physical benefits – here’s what to know.

It has been revealed that L-tyrosine is an amino acid that the body produces naturally. Though your bod can prob create enough of the stuff on its own, some research suggests that supplementing with it can boost your mood and help regulate your stress response.

L-tyrosine helps make many vital chemical messengers, such as:.

Supplementing with L-tyrosine is believed by some to boost levels of dopamine, adrenalin, and norepinephrine in particular.

Foods naturally high in tyrosine include:.

L-tyrosine may improve your memory and mental alertness. Since L-tyrosine increases dopamine availability in your body, experts think it may boost your cognitive performance. In addition to reward centers, dopamine is linked to working memory processes and plays a key role in the brain’s aging process.

Industry observers note that in a 2019 review of several studies, researchers found that a higher intake of L-tyrosine was linked to improved cognition. It also improved executive functions like brain flexibility, convergent thinking, and reasoning.

However, researchers noted that L-tyrosine is most effective when dopamine and norepinephrine levels are reduced (which basically means when you feel stressed AF).

Some L-tyrosine supplement companies claim that their products are both mood boosters and antidepressants, but the results are mixed.

L-tyrosine increases dopamine, the feel-good hormone that’s linked to reward processing and also addiction. In general, it’s been shown to be a vital regulator of mood, behavior, and brainpower – so it makes sense that getting enough of it could benefit your mood, too.

However, the research on supplementation of tyrosine for depression is super dated, so it’s challenging to draw any definitive conclusions RN. (Plus, depression is also a super complex condition that involves more than just dopamine depletion.).

Industry observers note that and though there are some people dubbing L-tyrosine “natural Adderall” for its purported beneficial effect on ADHD, so far, there’s no research to support these claims yet, either. (Though it *is* true that there seems to be a link between ADHD and altered dopamine levels.).

Phenylketonuria is a rare genetic disorder in which the body can’t properly process another essential amino acid, phenylalanine.

Since those with the disorder may also be deficient in L-tyrosine, some experts think that supplementing with it could help relieve some symptoms like seizures or skin rashes.

However, according to a 2021 review of several studies, there is not enough evidence to say for sure.

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) considers taking L-tyrosine supplements generally safe.

That being said, it’s not recommended to mix with the following medications:.

It’s not advisable to take it if you’re pregnant or breastfeeding.

Research suggests that L-tyrosine supplementation likely benefits your brainpower under stress. It also may benefit conditions like depression, but more research is needed to know for sure.

Like any supplement, it is a good idea to contact your healthcare provider before adding it to your medicine cabinet, especially if you have preexisting health conditions or take medications.

Logitech MX Keypad review: Can nine LCD keys take the pain out of Photoshop?
